extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutions seeking philanthropic research funding from Schmidt Sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level priorities describing what kinds of research and application routes Schmidt Sciences funds (thematic centers, preferred research character, submission mechanism). Useful for prospective applicants to determine fit and how to engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission policy (unsolicited proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: We proactively seek out grant opportunities and do not accept unsolicited proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not send unsolicited proposals; instead apply only to the foundation's listed open calls/RFPs. Engagement is via announced opportunities (e.g., specific 2026 RFPs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding mechanism: open calls and RFPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Please find our current open calls listed below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is distributed through time‑bound, topic‑specific open calls and requests for proposals (RFPs) such as the listed 2026 calls (AI for Actionable Matter Modeling; HAVI; Science of Trustworthy AI; Unconventional Compute; Research Frontiers Network). Prospective applicants must apply through those listed opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center-based thematic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Within each of our five centers, we organize scientific support through programs and projects—tailored to the needs of each specific hypothesis or challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects must align with one of the five centers and their respective missions; fit to a center and to a specific hypothesis/challenge is a key determinant of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority research areas (AI & Advanced Computing)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI & Advanced Computing — Supporting AI research and tools to accelerate breakthroughs across fields
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and tools that advance AI/advanced computing capabilities and enable cross‑disciplinary breakthroughs are prioritized under this center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority research areas (Astrophysics & Space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Astrophysics & Space — Unveiling the mysteries of the Universe with rapid realizations of innovative technology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that combines astrophysics questions with rapid technological realization (e.g., instrumentation, missions, telescopes) aligns with this center's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority research areas (Biosciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosciences — Harnessing biology's infinite possibilities at its intersection with chemistry, physics, and engineering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary bioscience projects at the intersection of biology, chemistry, physics, and engineering are in scope for this center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority research areas (Climate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate — Supporting climate research to bend the carbon curve and secure a sustainable future
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aiming to reduce emissions, improve climate understanding, or deliver scalable climate solutions align with this center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority research areas (Science Systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science Systems — Breaking down barriers to scientific discovery by supporting people, tools, and communities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives that strengthen scientific infrastructure, people, tools, or communities (e.g., workforce, platforms, collaborative networks) are prioritized here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred research character: boldness and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Bold science, deep and continuous collaborations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences favors ambitious, high‑impact scientific work carried out through sustained, deep collaborations rather than narrowly incremental or one‑off efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of supported research: basic to pressing problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Our team supports researchers pursuing hypotheses that address everything from basic‑science questions to pressing problems facing the planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both fundamental/basic research and problem‑driven applied research that addresses urgent societal or planetary challenges are within scope; applicants should articulate how their work fits on this spectrum.
